iterate-async / iterate — LLM / Agent Context File

What this is

iterate-async is a pipelined, concurrency-controlled async iterator
processor.

It is NOT: - a simple map helper - a queue - a wrapper around
Promise.all

It IS: - a pull-based, work-stealing pipeline over any iterable -
designed for uneven, streaming, or unbounded workloads - built to keep
workers busy at all times

Core mental model: → async processing pipeline with dynamic concurrency

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Core API

ProcessConcurrently(fn, iterable, options?) => Promise<Result[]> &
Instance

-   Returns a Promise you can await
-   Also exposes live runtime state

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Basic Usage

import ProcessConcurrently from ‘iterate-async’;

const results = await ProcessConcurrently( async (item) => item * 2, [1,
2, 3, 4] );

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Supported Inputs

Any iterable: - Array - Set - Map - String - Generator - Async
generator - Custom iterators

Key differentiator: → Works with infinite/lazy data sources

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Options

{ 
  concurrency?: number // default: 4 
  commonArgs?: any // passed to fn as 2nd arg 
  log?: ‘log’|‘info’|‘warn’|‘error’|fn 
  applyArgs?: (item, common, meta) => any[]
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Iterator Function Signature

async function fn(item, commonArgs, meta)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meta (live state)

{
  idx // index of current item 
  idxx // items dispatched so far 
  done // completed items 
  active // currently running 
  worker // worker slot id
  results // partial results snapshot
  signal // AbortSignal 
  waiting? // remaining items (if known) 
  total? // total items (if known)
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Runtime Instance

const job = ProcessConcurrently(fn, items);

Live properties: job.concurrency job.result job.done job.active job.idx
job.running job.errors job.waiting? job.total?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Dynamic Concurrency

job.concurrency = 10 job.concurrency = 2 job.concurrency = 0

Scaling DOWN aborts excess workers. Scaling UP increases throughput. 0
pauses execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Scheduling Model

Work-stealing pipeline (NOT chunking)

Workers continuously pull next item.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Why Pipeline > Chunking

Chunking: - waits for slowest item in batch - creates idle workers

Pipeline: - redistributes work dynamically - smooths uneven workloads

pipeline_time ≈ total_work / concurrency

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Lifecycle Hooks

class Worker { constructor({ signal, worker }) {} init() {} destroy() {}
async run(item, common, meta) {} }

------------------------------------------------------------------------

applyArgs

applyArgs: (item, common, meta) => [args…]

Use this when mapping with a pre-made function.

Bad:
```
// fn expects (url, method, body) instead of (item, common, meta)
const fn = async (url, method, body) => { ... };

await ProcessConcurrently(item => fn(item.url, item.method, item.body), requests});
```

Good:
```
// fn expects (url, method, body) instead of (item, common, meta)
const fn = async (url, method, body) => { ... };

await ProcessConcurrently(fn, requests, {
  applyArgs: (item, common, meta) => [item.url, item.method, item.body],
});
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Error Handling

-   Errors propagate
-   Stored in job.errors[index]

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Key Capabilities

-   dynamic concurrency
-   any iterable
-   streaming / infinite support
-   worker lifecycle hooks
-   live progress tracking
-   pause/resume
-   no dependencies

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Positioning

vs p-map: - batching vs streaming

vs p-limit: - primitive vs system

vs p-queue: - scheduler vs processor

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Examples

Fetch with concurrency limit

```
const results = await ProcessConcurrently(
  (id, { baseUrl }) => fetch(`${baseUrl}${id}`).then(r => r.json()),
  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
  { commonArgs: { baseUrl: 'https://api.example.com/items/' }, concurrency: 2 }
);
```

Read files in Node.js

```
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const buffers = await ProcessConcurrently(
  (filename, { dir }) => readFile(`${dir}/${filename}`),
  ['a.txt', 'b.txt', 'c.txt'],
  { commonArgs: { dir: './data' } }
);
```

Walk a directory tree with a generator

```js
import { readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';

function* walk(dir) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const path = `${dir}/${entry}`;
    if (statSync(path).isDirectory()) yield* walk(path);
    else yield path;
  }
}

const results = await ProcessConcurrently(uploadFile, walk('./src'), { concurrency: 8 });
```

Walk a directory tree with an async generator

```js
import { readdir, stat } from 'node:fs/promises';

async function* walk(dir) {
  for (const entry of await readdir(dir)) {
    const path = `${dir}/${entry}`;
    if ((await stat(path)).isDirectory()) yield* walk(path);
    else yield path;
  }
}

const results = await ProcessConcurrently(uploadFile, walk('./src'), { concurrency: 8 });
```

Progress indicator

```js
const fn = (item, { el }, meta) => {
  el.textContent = `${meta.done} / ${meta.total}`;
  return processItem(item);
};

await ProcessConcurrently(fn, items, {
  commonArgs: { el: document.querySelector('#progress') },
  concurrency: 4,
});
```

Silence logging

```js
await ProcessConcurrently(fn, items, { log: () => {} });
```

Use a custom logger

```js
await ProcessConcurrently(fn, items, { log: 'warn' });       // console.warn
await ProcessConcurrently(fn, items, { log: myLogger.info.bind(myLogger) }); // custom function
```

Error handling

```js
try {
  await ProcessConcurrently(fn, items);
} catch (e) {
  console.error(job.errors); // sparse array — only errored positions are set
}
```

Error handling - dynamic re-try

```
const items = [{i: 1, r: 0}, {i: 2, r: 0}, {i: 3, r: 0}, {i: 4, r: 0}];
const OK = Symbol('OK');
const ERROR = Symbol('ERROR');
await ProcessConcurrently(async (item) => {
  try {
    const result = await taskThatMightFail(item);
    return [OK, result]   
  } catch(e) {
    if(item.r < 10)
      items.push({...item, r: item.r + 1});
    return [ERROR, e];
  }
}, items);
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

When to Use

Use when: Mapping over *any* async workload

------------------------------------------------------------------------

One-liner

Process any iterable with a dynamically scalable async pipeline.
